items.new: But soon, returning to a horizontal position, Moby Dick swam swiftly round and round the wrecked crew, churning the water sideways in his vengeful wake, as if whipping himself up to yet another and deadlier attack. The sight of the splintered boat seemed to madden him, as the blood of grapes and mulberries, cast before Antiochus's elephants in the book of Maccabees, maddened them. Meanwhile Ahab was half smothered in the foam of the whale's insolent tail, and too much of a cripple to swim — though he could still keep afloat, even in the heart of a whirlpool like that — and helpless Ahab's head could be seen like a tossed bubble that the slightest chance shock might burst. From the broken-off stern of the boat Fedallah watched him with mild indifference; the clinging crew at the other drifting end could not help him; it was more than enough for them to look after themselves. For the White Whale's aspect as he revolved was so appalling, and the ever-tightening circles he made were so swift, like a planet's, that he seemed to be swooping horizontally upon them. And though the other boats, unharmed, still hovered close by, they dared not pull into the eddy to strike, for fear that would be the signal for the instant destruction of the endangered castaways, Ahab and all; nor in that case could they themselves hope to escape. So, with straining eyes, they stayed on the outer edge of the dreadful zone, whose center had now become the old man's head.

items.new: Let it be said here that this persistent pursuit of one particular whale, kept up through day into night and through night into day, is by no means unheard of in the South Sea fishery. For such is the wonderful skill, the foresight born of experience, and the unshakable confidence acquired by some great natural geniuses among the Nantucket captains, that from simply observing a whale when last sighted they will, under certain given circumstances, predict pretty accurately both the direction in which he will keep swimming for a while out of sight, and his probable rate of progress during that time. In these cases the whale-fisherman does somewhat as a pilot does when he is about to lose sight of a coast whose general trend he knows well, and which he wants to return to shortly, but at some further point: just as this pilot stands by his compass and takes the exact bearing of the cape now in view, so as to be surer of hitting the remote, unseen headland he will eventually reach, so the fisherman stands at his compass with the whale; for after the creature has been chased and carefully marked through several hours of daylight, then, when night hides the fish, its future wake through the darkness is almost as settled in the hunter's shrewd mind as the pilot's coast is in his. So, to this hunter's wondrous skill, a wake — that proverbially fleeting thing written in water — is for all desired purposes nearly as reliable as the steadfast land. And just as the mighty iron Leviathan of the modern railway is so familiarly known in its every pace that men, watches in hand, time his rate as doctors time a baby's pulse, and say casually that the up train or the down train will reach such and such a spot at such and such an hour, so, almost, there are occasions when these Nantucketers time that other Leviathan of the deep by the observed humor of his speed, and say to themselves that so many hours from now this whale will have gone two hundred miles, and will have about reached this or that degree of latitude or longitude. But for this sharpness to succeed at all in the end, the wind and the sea must be the whaleman's allies; for what use at the moment to the becalmed or windbound sailor is the skill that assures him he is exactly ninety-three leagues and a quarter from his port? Many further subtle points concerning the chase of whales can be inferred from these statements.

items.new: As if to strike quick terror into them — being by this time the first to attack — Moby Dick had turned and was now coming for the three crews. Ahab's boat was in the center; and cheering his men on, he told them he would take the whale head-and-head — that is, pull straight up to his forehead — which is not an uncommon thing; for within a certain distance such a course keeps the coming attack out of the whale's sideways vision. But before that close range was reached, and while all three boats were still as plain to his eye as the ship's three masts, the White Whale, churning himself into a furious speed, rushed among the boats almost in an instant, as it were, with open jaws and lashing tail, and offered appalling battle on every side; and heedless of the irons darted at him from every boat, he seemed intent only on annihilating each separate plank those boats were made of. But skillfully maneuvered, wheeling ceaselessly like trained war-horses on the field, the boats evaded him for a while, though at times only by a plank's breadth; while all the time Ahab's unearthly war cry tore every other cry but his to shreds.

items.new: "Forehead to forehead I meet you, this third time, Moby Dick! On deck there! — brace sharper up; crowd her into the wind's eye. He's too far off to lower yet, Mr. Starbuck. The sails shake! Stand over that helmsman with a top-maul! So, so; he travels fast, and I must go down. But let me have one more good round look aloft here at the sea; there's time for that. An old, old sight, and yet somehow so young; aye, and not changed a wink since I first saw it, a boy, from the sand-hills of Nantucket! The same! — the same! — the same to Noah as to me. There's a soft shower to leeward. Such lovely leewardings! They must lead somewhere — to something other than common land, more palmy than the palms. Leeward! The white whale goes that way; look to windward, then; the better if the bitterer quarter. But good-bye, good-bye, old masthead! What's this? — green? Aye, tiny mosses in these warped cracks. No such green weather-stains on Ahab's head! There's the difference now between man's old age and matter's. But aye, old mast, we both grow old together; sound in our hulls, though, are we not, my ship? Aye, minus a leg, that's all. By heaven, this dead wood has the better of my live flesh every way. I can't compare with it; and I've known some ships made of dead trees outlast the lives of men made of the most vital stuff of vital fathers. What's that he said? He should still go before me, my pilot, and yet be seen again? But where? Will I have eyes at the bottom of the sea, supposing I go down those endless stairs? And all night I've been sailing away from him, wherever he sank to. Aye, aye, like many more, you told dire truth about yourself, O Parsee; but, Ahab, there your shot fell short. Good-bye, masthead — keep a good eye on the whale while I'm gone. We'll talk tomorrow — no, tonight, when the white whale lies down there, tied by head and tail."

items.new: It so happened that after the Parsee's disappearance, I was the one whom the Fates ordained to take the place of Ahab's bowsman, when that bowsman assumed the vacant post; and I was the same one who, on the last day, when the three men were tossed out of the rocking boat, was dropped astern. So, floating on the margin of the scene that followed, and in full sight of it, when the half-spent suction of the sunken ship reached me, I was drawn, but slowly, toward the closing vortex. When I reached it, it had subsided to a creamy pool. Round and round, then, and ever contracting toward the button-like black bubble at the axis of that slowly wheeling circle, I revolved like another Ixion. Then, as I reached that vital center, the black bubble burst upward; and now, released by its cunning spring, and, owing to its great buoyancy, rising with great force, the coffin life-buoy shot lengthwise from the sea, fell over, and floated by my side. Buoyed up by that coffin, for almost one whole day and night, I floated on a soft and dirgelike sea. The unharming sharks glided by as if with padlocks on their mouths; the savage sea-hawks sailed with sheathed beaks. On the second day, a sail drew near, nearer, and picked me up at last. It was the devious-cruising Rachel, that in her retracing search after her missing children, only found another orphan.
